name: Apache CouchDB
tagline: HTTP/JSON document database built around multi-master replication and offline-first sync.
description: Apache CouchDB stores JSON documents and exposes everything, including queries, replication and admin, over a plain HTTP REST API. Its defining feature is a robust replication protocol that lets any two CouchDB-compatible nodes sync bidirectionally, with MVCC revision trees for conflict detection. That makes it the backbone of offline-first stacks built with PouchDB and of IBM Cloudant. Queries use Mango (JSON selectors) or incremental MapReduce views, and Nouveau adds Lucene full-text search. Version 3.5.3 shipped in October 2026. It is steady, well-understood technology, best when sync and availability matter more than ad-hoc query power.

pricing.notes: Free; IBM Cloudant is the main managed CouchDB-compatible service.

scale.notes: Clustered mode shards each database (q shards, n replicas); cross-region topologies are built with continuous replication.

strengths: Bidirectional, resumable replication between any CouchDB-protocol peers, including PouchDB in browsers
Everything is HTTP + JSON, so curl is a complete client
Append-only storage is crash-safe; no repair step after power loss
_changes feed makes building sync and event pipelines straightforward
Permissive Apache license under neutral ASF governance
weaknesses: No multi-document transactions; conflicts must be resolved by the application
MapReduce views are slow to build on large databases
Compaction is needed to reclaim disk from the append-only files
Mango queries are far less expressive than SQL or the MongoDB aggregation pipeline
useCases: Offline-first web and mobile apps with PouchDB
Field data collection in low-connectivity environments
Multi-site replication between edge locations and a central hub
Document stores where HTTP-native access is valuable
notIdealFor: Transactional workloads that span multiple documents
Very high write rates on a single database
